findings.required_change: Replace with: Perform acquisition planning for every acquisition. Apply the current DoD/Navy rules to determine whether a written plan, streamlined plan, or other record is required; the coursebook $10M cue is not a universal contract-action threshold. Development, production/services, contract risk and local approval requirements differ. Cite new FAR-Overhaul-Part7-2026 and DoD-RFO-Deviation-Part7-2026.
findings.source_basis: RFO FAR 7.102; DFARS RFO 207.103-70; coursebook p9
findings.explanation: RFO development threshold is program total $10M or more, production/services $50M total/$25M per FY, and FAR requires written plans for cost-reimbursement/high-risk contracts. Avoid claiming full-current Navy threshold review without current signed attachment.

findings.original_claim: Contractor may not exceed the ceiling at its own risk.
findings.required_change: Use: The contractor exceeds the stated cost ceiling at its own risk unless the KO approves an increase; applicable limitation-of-cost or limitation-of-funds provisions govern notice and continued performance. Cite FAR-16-301-1-Cost-Reimbursement and new FAR-Overhaul-Part16-2026.
findings.explanation: The guide dropped the word except and reversed the source.

findings.original_claim: FFP price not subject to adjustment.
findings.required_change: Use: FFP price is not adjusted because of the contractor's cost experience; authorized changes and other applicable contract clauses can still change the price. Cite FAR-16-202-1-FFP.
findings.explanation: Keep cost-risk teaching without implying no modification can change an FFP price.

findings.original_claim: Guide repeats older SBIR typical ranges without current no-waiver ceiling.
findings.required_change: After phase descriptions use: As of 16 October 2026, SBA's no-waiver ceilings, including modifications, are $335,937 for Phase I and $2,239,578 for Phase II. The solicitation controls actual award amount and duration; Phase III uses non-SBIR/STTR funds. Cite SBA-SBIR-Limits-20261016; cross-reference R&D chapter.
findings.explanation: Earlier correction in R&D was not propagated into this chapter.

findings.original_claim: Data-rights summary omits negotiated, SBIR and commercial licenses; private funding framed as absolute limited rights.
findings.required_change: Add: Funding is a starting point, not the only rights rule. Form/fit/function and specified operation, maintenance, installation and training data may carry unlimited rights. GPR permits Government-purpose competition during its term, then normally converts to unlimited rights. Limited-rights exceptions permit specified emergency repair/overhaul and covered support-contractor access with safeguards. Negotiated licenses tailor rights; SBIR/STTR data uses its special clause; commercial technical data and commercial software use their respective licenses. Delivery obligations and license rights must both be acquired. Cite new DFARS-252-227-7013-2026 plus coursebook pp51-55; use 7014/7015/7018/227.7202 when adding detailed rules.
findings.explanation: Corrects p53 erroneous delay of competitive use until expiry and covers all substantive table categories without copying inaccurate blanket permissions.

findings.original_claim: Both IFB and RFP use UCF.
findings.guide_location: Solicitation, Evaluation, and Award Phase; Uniform Contract Format Essentials
findings.required_change: Use: The UCF is a common organization for covered solicitations; apply the format and exceptions required by the procurement procedure. RFO Part 15 places RFP structure at 15.102 and UCF at 15.109. Parts I-III form the physical award; Part IV stays in the file, with applicable representations/certifications incorporated by reference. Cite FAR-Overhaul-Part15-2026.
findings.explanation: Not every acquisition uses UCF; guide omits important visual distinction between solicitation and resulting contract.

findings.original_claim: Three indefinite-delivery contract types only named.
findings.required_change: Add: Definite quantity fixes quantity for a stated period with deliveries as ordered; IDIQ establishes a minimum and maximum for orders during a fixed period; a requirements contract covers the designated Government activity's actual purchase requirements during the stated period. Cite FAR-16-501-2-Indefinite-Delivery and coursebook p40.
findings.explanation: Restores meaningful distinctions asked by TLO 4.

findings.original_claim: Exercise lists scenarios without reasoned answer.
findings.required_change: Add: Defined repeat work and reliable estimates support considering FFP. A first-of-class overhaul with unvalidated estimates supports considering a cost-reimbursement or appropriately structured incentive arrangement if its prerequisites are met. Prior relationship alone does not select a type; justify the choice by scope certainty, measurable incentives, accounting adequacy and surveillance. Cite coursebook p39 and FAR-16-103-Negotiating-Contract-Type.
findings.explanation: Provides usable learning rationale without inventing one mandatory answer.

findings.original_claim: Phase diagram retains ICD/draft CDD/CDD-V/CDD with no legacy warning.
findings.required_change: Add to caption: Legacy requirements labels are retained only as part of the coursebook graphic; use current JFRP tailored SRD/ICD and SRD/CDD terminology and approval rules in the requirements chapter. This diagram is a notional risk-to-contract-type illustration.
